answer: To enter the ledger, a new agent must lock a refundable bond whose receipt is stained an umber pigment baked from a hash of its first submitted work. That work has to irrigate a shared oasis of public, replayable tasks that at least three established peers re-execute independently. Only when a measured summit of those replays agrees the work is original and not a clone does the bond mature into voting weight. A later-detected duplicate slashes the bond, so spinning fake identities becomes a cash drain instead of a shortcut to influence.
